own_solution.law: photon energy E = hc/lambda = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV; photon rate N = P/E; I = eta N e = eta P/(E/e) = 0.003 * 5e-3 W / 3.1 V
assumptions: photon energy exceeds the work function

T9477.regime: work function below the photon energy 3.1 eV (photoemission possible); 1.9 eV is inside

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The R sentences TD93A and T22AD add 3.4 mW from a second/further lamp without stating its wavelength (or that it is the same 400 nm light with the same 0.003 photon-to-electron probability), so the extra photon rate and hence the current are not determined; 8.129 uA holds only if the extra light is also 400 nm.

counterexamples: If the second lamp emitted at 600 nm (2.07 eV > 1.9 eV) with the same yield, the extra current would be 0.003*3.4e-3/2.067 = 4.93 uA, total 9.77 uA instead of 8.13 uA; if it emitted beyond the threshold (>653 nm for 1.9 eV) it would add nothing.
notes: e cancels: I = eta P e lambda/(hc) with hc in eV nm gives I = eta P/(3.1 V). Work function 1.9 eV: threshold 1240/1.9 = 652.6 nm > 400 nm, so K. Variant groups (3.4 mW; 1.9 eV; 'a little') consistent in number and unit.
